RoomType.rationale: FabricatorNormal.cs:15 `RoomType => RoomType.Monster`. Modeled structurally by pool membership. One shared mechanism across this batch; see `encounter/_room_type_and_weak` in the report.

HasScene.rationale: Presentation only -- gates a bespoke combat `.tscn` (FabricatorNormal.cs:17). No scene loading in the headless sim.

Slots.rationale: FabricatorNormal.cs:19 `Slots => ["bot1","bot2","fabricator","bot3","bot4"]`; `FABRICATOR_NORMAL = Encounter(..., slots=("bot1","bot2","fabricator","bot3","bot4"), monster_slots=("fabricator",))` (fabricator.py:232-240) is element-for-element identical, including the Fabricator seated in the MIDDLE entry rather than first. This is the fix already shipped and audited under `audit/records/monster/fabricator.json`'s guard "Encounter.GetNextSlot placement... has no sim analogue" (closed 2026-07-29, round 7) -- matched here per rule 3, not re-derived: that closure ported exactly this `Slots`/`monster_slots`/`get_next_slot` machinery, and this record's own reading of `Encounter.slots`/`monster_slots` (monsters/base.py:352-397) confirms it is still in place and unchanged since.

AllPossibleMonsters.issue: FabricatorNormal.cs:21-44 returns the Fabricator plus every bot in `Fabricator.defenseSpawns`/`aggroSpawns` (5 monster models total: Fabricator, Guardbot, Noisebot, Zapbot, Stabbot) as the declared superset of everything this encounter could ever field, including creatures that only ever appear via a MID-COMBAT spawn (never via `GenerateMonsters`). Shared finding, filed once under `encounter/_all_possible_monsters` (see `encounter/aeonglass` for the full enumeration of the three game-side debug/UI consumers; dormant, no sim counterpart to any of them). Distinct from `encounter/construct_menagerie`'s instance of the same shared gap in that this unit's superset genuinely differs in KIND, not just count, from its `GenerateMonsters` roster -- still costs nothing observable, for the same reason (no dev console, no stats screen, no bestiary in the headless sim).

GenerateMonsters.rationale: ROSTER: FabricatorNormal.cs:46-49 returns exactly one `(Fabricator, "fabricator")` pair -- the bots in `AllPossibleMonsters` are NOT part of the initial roster, they are summoned later by the Fabricator's own move (`monster/fabricator.json`'s subject, not this record's); `FABRICATOR_NORMAL = Encounter(..., monster_classes=[Fabricator], ...)` (fabricator.py:232-240) -- one monster, same class. ORDER: trivially matches (single element). SLOT: `"fabricator"` on both sides -- see the Slots hook above. DRAW COUNT: zero on both sides -- `FabricatorNormal.GenerateMonsters` never touches `base.Rng` (the Fabricator's bot-spawning RNG draws are its own MOVE, on the MonsterAi stream, already audited faithful in `monster/fabricator.json`'s guard on `Fabricator._spawn_bot`), and the sim's fixed-composition path draws nothing here (monsters/base.py:408-411).

GetCameraScaling.rationale: Presentation only. FabricatorNormal.cs:51-54 returns 0.85f. No camera in the headless sim.

GetCameraOffset.rationale: Presentation only. FabricatorNormal.cs:56-59 returns Vector2.Down*60f. No camera in the headless sim.

ShouldReceiveCombatHooks.rationale: `EncounterModel.ShouldReceiveCombatHooks => false` (EncounterModel.cs:39), not overridden. The sim's `Encounter` dataclass is never registered with `HookSystem` -- never a hook listener on either side.

guards.what: Draw count / stream independence of the per-encounter Rng
guards.rationale: Zero draws in GenerateMonsters (see above). The Fabricator's own in-combat bot-spawning draws are a MONSTER-tier (MonsterAi stream) concern, already audited in `monster/fabricator.json`, not re-derived here.

guards.what: The Niche HP-roll (Fabricator has min_hp==max_hp==150, degenerate range, single initial enemy)
guards.rationale: Same shape as `encounter/aeonglass`'s check: one draw on both sides for the initial Fabricator (`hashSet={150}` -> `NextItem`; sim `candidates=[150]` -> `next_int_range(0,1)`, combat.py:402-422). Each bot the Fabricator later summons rolls its OWN Niche HP via `CombatState.assign_parity_hp` (combat.py:438-446, the mid-combat-spawn path), already checked faithful in `monster/fabricator.json`'s and `power/stock.json`'s guards on the identical mechanism -- not re-derived here.
rooms.py:265 lists `fabricator` in Glory's `normal_keys`, and `FABRICATOR_NORMAL` is registered in `sts2_rl/monsters/glory/__init__.py`'s `ENCOUNTERS` dict (line 64).
